name: plan-eng-review
conclusion_quantitative: plan-eng-review (Act) specifies 5 of 5 categories: 2 autonomy limits, 10+ clarification rules, 3 approval gates, 1 validation rule, 6 escalation rules. Strongest: clarification rules.
conclusion_qualitative: plan-eng-review reviews an implementation plan the way an engineering manager would (architecture, code quality, tests and performance) before any code is written. Most of its rules make the agent consult the user, one question per issue and before assuming any direction, and it asks for confirmation before upgrades, opening links and setting the evaluation scope. It may move on alone only when the scope check finds nothing overbuilt. It requires evidence before calling work done, and stops and escalates after repeated failures, on security doubts, or when it cannot verify the work.

autonomy_limits.conclusion_quantitative: 2 autonomy limits (2 mandatory, 0 advisory; 2 conditional), mostly prose.
autonomy_limits.conclusion_qualitative: There are 2 rules, both strict, both tied to a situation, both in running text. When proactive mode is off, the agent runs gstack skills only when the user explicitly asks. If its scope check finds the plan is not overbuilt, it presents its findings and moves on to the review without asking.

statements.quote: If `PROACTIVE` is `"false"`, do not proactively suggest gstack skills — only invoke them when the user explicitly asks.
If the complexity check does not trigger, present your Step 0 findings and proceed directly to Section 1.

clarification_rules.conclusion_quantitative: 10+ clarification rules (10 mandatory, 0 advisory; 3 conditional), mostly prose.
clarification_rules.conclusion_qualitative: There are 10 or more rules (the first 10 are kept), all strict, 3 tied to a situation, mostly running text. The agent asks the user about telemetry during setup, says exactly what it needs when information is missing, and asks for the user's input on every issue instead of assuming a direction. When the plan looks overbuilt it asks whether to reduce scope. After each review section it stops, asks one question per issue and goes on only when all are resolved, and it presents each possible TODO as its own question.

validation.conclusion_quantitative: 1 validation rule (1 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly list.
validation.conclusion_qualitative: There is one strict rule, always on, in a bullet point. A task counts as done only when every step is complete with evidence for each claim.

statements.quote: **DONE** — All steps completed successfully. Evidence provided for each claim.

escalation.conclusion_quantitative: 6 escalation rules (5 mandatory, 1 advisory; 3 conditional), mostly list.
escalation.conclusion_qualitative: There are 6 rules, 5 strict and 1 counted as a suggestion (it contains "should"), 3 tied to a situation, mostly bullet points. The agent reports concerns or blockers, saying what blocks it and what it tried. It may always stop and say a task is too hard, and it must stop and escalate after 3 failed attempts, when unsure about a security-sensitive change, or when the work goes beyond what it can verify.

statements.quote: **DONE_WITH_CONCERNS** — Completed, but with issues the user should know about. List each concern.
**BLOCKED** — Cannot proceed. State what is blocking and what was tried.
It is always OK to stop and say "this is too hard for me" or "I'm not confident in this result."
If you have attempted a task 3 times without success, STOP and escalate.
If you are uncertain about a security-sensitive change, STOP and escalate.
If the scope of work exceeds what you can verify, STOP and escalate.
